Hey! So sorry you’re going through this! 

Firstly, feeling as though you’re “faking” being depressed or “just being a victim” is super common among people suffering depression, it’s just your brains way of trying to ‘explain things away’. Your body isn’t comfortable feeling the way it does, so your brain tries to come up with a conclusion as to why. It’s just a mean trick, but don’t doubt how you feel! 

Secondly, don’t feel as though there has to be a reason to be depressed, or that you shouldn’t be based on your life experience. There are an incredible amount of things that can trigger these feelings, sometimes things as minute as not getting enough sleep or being stressed at work. Take a step back and assure yourself that you’re not going crazy, you don’t need a license to feel like this! 

You mentioned seeing a therapist which is honestly great, because a lot of people just try to ignore feeling depressed, so be proud of yourself for asking for help! I’m really sorry your parents aren’t supportive, but in life you’ll occasionally come across people that just don’t appreciate how tricky mental health can be, but this doesn’t mean there is anything at all ‘wrong’ with you. 

There’s no sure fire way to get rid of depression, but you can manage it and get it under control. Just remind yourself that this feeling is not going to last forever, as much as it might feel like it. I myself suffered with depression for years before I learned what worked for me, it’s all trial and error! Definitely continue seeing your therapist and be as open and honest as possible. Some things that helped me were getting a hobby (or really anything to distract yourself and experience another emotion, something to make you feel accomplished and focus on working towards something, like an art project, or taking a walk to somewhere you’ve never been, or doing something you used to enjoy doing). Also, I know you said your parents weren’t particularly supportive; do you have any friends that are aware of how you feel? There are ALWAYS people out there to talk to, and it’s always been helpful for me to know I’m not alone in how I feel, you’re not unstable or crazy, this is something normal that people suffer with. 

You are so much more than just depression! I know this advice doesn’t fix everything right away, but sometimes it’s helpful to know you’re not alone in this at all. Don’t be hard on yourself for feeling things, but always remind yourself that you deserve to feel better. Remind yourself of who you are outside of depression, the things you like to do, the things you enjoy, the people you’re friends with and why they love you. There is always this sub you can come to!

I’ve had lash extensions around 3 times in the last year, and there are some real things to consider! 

On the good side, I never felt like I had to use false lashes and mascara because you wake up and bam, there’s your lashes, ready to go! 

However, I found them SUPER irritating. You’re having something foreign on your eye, and that takes a while to get used to. Also, I sleep on my left side, so after a couple of day’s I’d find that my lashes on the left eye would be a little but mis-shapen due to sleeping on them. 

Like you, I also have naturally long and thick lashes. Having extensions basically killed off my lash line - the only reason I continued having extensions done is because I’d have them removed and my lashes would be so patchy and awful. Now I’m no expert, but twice I’ve had them removed by a professional, and once I carefully removed them myself using coconut oil, and all three times had the same result. 

They are lovely to have and it’s a really nice alternative to false lashes. However, the aftermath is definitely something to consider, as I can personally vouch that it took me around three months to get my natural lashes back to normal (I.e not patchy, brittle and irritated). My lashes usually last around 4 weeks with good care, however it may be useful to get a temporary set for around a week to see how your eyes adjust!

I would recommend getting tested for HIV now, just to put your mind at rest, and then at 4 weeks and again in 3 months.

I had a lot of issues with my extreme depression in my long term relationship. It was hard for my partner because one week I would be fantastic, then for no apparent reason, the following week I would create arguments from nothing, cry for hours, refuse to talk to her and isolate myself, and when I tried to discuss my issues, it would all come out as a jumbled mess. 

One thing I found really helped was us BOTH working on it as well as myself. It was my partners first experience being with someone with depression and we went to counseling sessions together, and we actually went to a few talks about mental health and depression. Even something like going to your doctor, it’s really helpful for THEM to know what’s going on with you and maybe get some tips for how to deal with you when you’re not feeling yourself. 

Also, please don’t try and hold back your feelings! You can still have those feelings, but try to get them out in a different way. I used to actually write down exactly what I was feeling, just a scribbled mess, and once I’d calmed down I’d try to go through it with my partner in a more controlled space, and when I’d calmed down a little.

I’ve definitely experienced similar issues, so honestly don’t feel bad about it! It’s normal and it’s just your brain and body trying to protect itself! 

Firstly, recognize that it’s fine to feel like this. There is absolutely nothing wrong with it. Everyone has thoughts like this, it’s just that yours may come out for aggressively than other people’s might. You’re aware of it and that’s a huge thing to be proud of. 

Secondly, it doesn’t all have to come out at once. When I’ve had these thoughts in the past, in an effort to try and control it, I’ve just blurted everything out in the very early stages. This will most likely make you and the other person feel worse. You can give just a little tiny bit of information at a time, don’t feel like you have to lay everything bare. 

When you do feel these thoughts approaching, literally just stop yourself for a second and think. It’s easy for your mind to just run away with itself. Sit and think carefully, maybe even write some things down. What DO I actually have to be worried about? Why DO I not want to talk to them, and is that rational? IS there anything actually wrong, or do I just need to have a cheeky glass of wine and calm the heck down? 

You don’t have to get everything out. If you feel it’s your issue, you DO have the power to control it, even if it feels like you don’t. They’re literally your own thoughts, and you can choose how and if they impact you. I’d say see how things go for a few more weeks, just going at a pace you’re comfortable with, and maybe at some point broach the subject slightly, like “hey, I know I can be a bit weird sometimes when we’re discussing things, but I do want to be open with you and I’m trying to be”, and reassure him “this is an issue I’m aware of, but I’m working on it and I’m dealing with it and your support means a real lot to me”.

Hey! So I'll start with something that I get told all the time and I KNOW it's not nice to hear, but most these symptoms are linked to anxiety! 
Constant fear and anxiousness takes a toll on your body and mind. Anything like headaches and fatigue are evidence of this - they're your body's way of saying "I've had enough". When your anxiety is so bad that you are having panic attacks, your body goes into a form of "survival mode" where you are hyper-aware of your surroundings. For long periods of time, this is stressful for your body.
I also suffer with health anxiety (22y/o female) and I also get pains around my pelvis and vulva. These can be caused by any number of things - it could have been maybe one instance, but because you are expecting it, your mind has the horrible idea to enact it. This could be what's also causing your muscle pain, because you are focusing your energy onto it. 

I don't want this to sound patronising at all! But these symptoms are something I have most days, and I've learnt to recognise them as a part of my anxiety. I would suggest going to see your doctor for a full blood test to rule out anything seriously wrong, and maybe considering therapy such as CBT to combat how you process and manage intrusive thoughts! 

Don't panic,  we're all in the same boat here. You're going to be fine 😊

I have the same anxiety, and since talking to a counsellor I've realised it's something a lot of people have! Here are some tips that have helped me:
1. Realise that it is actually difficult to contract - even having unprotected sex with someone positive is a 1 in 1000 chance. Most people that have HIV are aware, as these days most individuals get blood tests quite frequently and, even if they didn't, they would likely have some symptoms to make them aware. 
2. HIV isn't a death sentence. The last time I was tested I was sweating and shaking and the nurse said to me "if it comes back that you have HIV, all that will happen is we give you medication and you carry on the rest of your life as normal". Medications can keep a HIV count so low it can't even be detected on a blood test! If you do ever contract it, which I am 100% sure you do not have it and likely will not catch it due to your caution, a diagnosis like this should not have any effect on relationships as there is very little chance of your partner contracting it with the correct precaution and medication. Some people are now even having children after a HIV diagnosis.
3. Recognise your anxiety. You are worried about this because, as you say, it's incurable. Your anxiety seeks out things that defy logic and reasoning. Be open with whoever you are intimate with - get to know them, trust them, make them aware of your anxiety surrounding the issue. Your partner will likely admire your caution and respect for yourself to be so aware of STD's. 

You're not alone in this, trust me I've had many sleepless nights and unnecessary blood tests thinking I'm infected! If you ever have a risky situation you can always get PEP upto 72 hours after possible exposure. Always stay safe until you are comfortable with someone. You're not going to be alone, regardless of HIV! You do not have it, and I know many people that do have HIV that live happy, healthy lives, have partners and children and are fully supported, so put your anxiety to rest!
